learning: Hypothesis: the wider span keeps the tape in view on sharp bends and cuts line loss below 2.0. If line loss reaches 0 but max_error stays at or above 0.06, the limit is turning authority, and narrowing wheel_track is the next lever. If steering_oscillation rises well above 0.25, the wider span is reducing signal sensitivity and kd needs to rise.
notes: Runs the Builder's 60 mm span at y = 0.075 m with the iteration-4 controller unchanged, so the span change is the only variable. Watch line_loss_events and max_error on the s-bend and slalom.
rationale: Iteration 4 is the best design so far (score 291.9). It ran the oval to 15 of 20 finishes (mean progress 0.81, mean finish time 1.64 s) with kd 0.4 and y = 0.075 m. The s-bend and slalom still lost the line in all 40 runs, with line_loss_events at 2.0 on both and max_error at 0.072 and 0.066. Line loss is still at least 1 on every track, so the advance rule applies: the array stays at the forward limit (y = 0.075 m) and the span widens from 50 mm to 60 mm (x = ±0.03 m), as the Geometry Builder proposed. I keep the controller identical to iteration 4 (kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]) so the race isolates the span change. The 15 mm sensor spacing still overlaps the 12 mm footprints. Base speed stays at 1.4 because the oval finishes in 1.64 s and the failures on the bends are off-track losses, not a lack of speed, so raising speed now would likely worsen them. Expected result: line_loss_events below 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom, and a score above 291.9. Risk: a wider span may reduce signal sensitivity near centre, so steering_oscillation and rms_error are the watch points.
